subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Show that the curves 6x² − 5x + 2y = 0 and 4x² + 8y² = 3 touch each other at (1/2, 1/2).

mark_split.label: Check the point lies on both curves
Find the slope of the first curve there
Find the slope of the second curve there
Show the two slopes are equal

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you check first about the given point, and say what touch each other means in terms of the slopes.

steps.label: Check the point lies on both curves
steps.margin_note: First mark. Touching is a statement about a COMMON point, so the point has to be shown to be on both curves before any slope is found. This is a scoring line, not a formality.
lines: ∴ P(1/2, 1/2) lies on both curves, so it is a common point.

recall.must_convey: That (1/2, 1/2) is substituted into both equations and satisfies both, so it is a common point.
accept: substitute half and half into both equations first
check the point lies on both curves
six into one fourth minus five into half plus one is zero

it is a common point so the curves meet there

steps.why: Equal slopes at two different points would say nothing at all. Touching means the curves share a point AND share the tangent there, so the shared point is half the statement being proved.
common_mistakes: Going straight to the derivatives without checking the point.
Checking the point on one curve only.
Arithmetic slip with 6(1/4) written as 6/2 instead of 3/2.
steps.memory_tip: Touching needs two things: the same point and the same slope. Prove them in that order.

steps.label: Find the slope of the first curve there
steps.margin_note: Second mark. In (i) the y-term is 2y, so its derivative is simply 2·dy/dx. The slope comes out in x alone, so only x = 1/2 is needed.

recall.must_convey: That differentiating 6x² − 5x + 2y = 0 gives dy/dx = (5 − 12x)/2, so m₁ = −1/2 at x = 1/2.
accept: differentiate the first curve to get twelve x minus five plus two dy by dx
dy by dx is five minus twelve x by two
m one is minus one half
modati curve slope x meeda maatrame aadhaarapadutundi
put x equal to half to get minus half
five minus six by two is minus one by two

steps.why: The first curve is already solved for y up to a factor, so its slope depends on x only. That makes the check quick and independent of the y-coordinate.
common_mistakes: Differentiating 2y as 2 without the dy/dx factor.
Writing dy/dx = (12x − 5)/2 with the sign reversed.
steps.memory_tip: Every y-term picks up dy/dx behind it; every pure x-term does not.

steps.label: Find the slope of the second curve there
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Here 8y² differentiates to 16y·dy/dx. Cancelling the 8 gives the compact form −x/(2y), which is fastest to evaluate.

recall.must_convey: That differentiating 4x² + 8y² = 3 gives dy/dx = −x/(2y), so m₂ = −1/2 at (1/2, 1/2).
accept: differentiate the second curve to get eight x plus sixteen y dy by dx
dy by dx is minus x by two y
m two is minus one half

eight by sixteen cancels to one by two
substitute half and half to get minus half

steps.why: This curve is an ellipse and its slope needs both coordinates, so the y-value from step 1 is used here. Simplifying −8x/(16y) before substituting avoids a fraction inside a fraction.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the derivative of the constant 3 is 0.
Writing the slope as −2x/y by cancelling the wrong way.
steps.memory_tip: For Ax² + By² = C the slope is −Ax/(By): here A = 4 and B = 8, so it is −4x/(8y) = −x/(2y).

steps.label: Show the two slopes are equal
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Touch each other means the curves share the point AND share the tangent, that is m₁ = m₂. State both halves of the conclusion.
lines: Two curves touch each other at a common point when their slopes there are equal.
m₁ = −1/2  and  m₂ = −1/2, so  m₁ = m₂
The common tangent at P(1/2, 1/2) is

lines.text: ∴ P(1/2, 1/2) lies on both curves and both have slope −1/2 there, so the curves touch each other at (1/2, 1/2).

recall.must_convey: That m₁ = m₂ = −1/2, so the curves have the same tangent at the common point and therefore touch.

steps.why: Equal slopes alone would only mean the tangents are parallel. Together with the common point from step 1, equal slopes mean one shared tangent line, which is what touching is.
common_mistakes: Using m₁m₂ = −1, which is the test for cutting at right angles, not for touching.
Concluding from equal slopes alone without mentioning the common point.
Putting the two slopes into the angle formula and reporting θ = 0 without saying what it means.
steps.memory_tip: Same point and same slope means one tangent serves both curves — that single shared tangent is what touching means.

insider_note: Touching means the point lies on BOTH curves and the slopes agree there — two separate checks. Verify membership first, then compare the two derivatives.
